**Ch 004 draft analysis**

The draft is a tight but coherent compression. The Narcissus paragraph opens with "And still deeper the meaning of that story of Narcissus" — in the source this follows an extended water-meditation chain (Prairies, Niagara, Tennessee poet, etc.) that built to this culmination. The draft cuts all those examples but keeps "Yes, as every one knows, meditation and water are wedded for ever" reduced to "Meditation and water are wedded for ever," then immediately pivots to "And still deeper the meaning of that story of Narcissus." The word "still deeper" implies a comparative escalation from the preceding passage — but the preceding draft passage is only the single sentence about meditation and water. A reader can still parse the sentence; "still deeper" merely reads as emphatic rather than comparative. This is a less-ornamented version, not a structural failure.

The schoolmaster transition: "The transition is a keen one, from a schoolmaster to a sailor" — the source establishes this by saying "just previous to putting your hand into the tar-pot, you have been lording it as a country schoolmaster." The draft cut that setup but mentions "schoolmaster" directly in the transition sentence itself, so the referent is present in the sentence. No structural damage.

No valid findings in Ch 004.

---

**Ch 005 draft analysis**

"Wretched entertainment at the sign of 'The Trap!' muttered I, backing out." — In the source, the inn is named "The Trap" because Ishmael reasons: the other places were "The Crossed Harpoons" and "The Sword-Fish Inn," so this must be "The Trap." That deductive naming joke is cut from the draft. The draft uses the name "The Trap" without any prior establishment of it as a name. A reader sees Ishmael enter a building whose sign was never named "The Trap" in the draft — the draft only said "a smoky light from a low, wide building." The name appears for the first time in the muttered line, with no antecedent in the draft. However, looking closely: the source's logic is a wry joke, and the draft's Ishmael still mutters "The Trap" as his own coinage for the place. A competent reader would understand "The Trap" as Ishmael's sardonic nickname for this dismal church — the referent (the building he just entered) is clear. Not a structural failure by the gate test.

"Poor Lazarus there, chattering his teeth against the curbstone—that he should lie stranded before the door of Dives is more wonderful than that an iceberg should be moored to one of the Moluccas." — In the source, Lazarus and Dives are introduced in an extended passage comparing the freezing poor man on the curbstone to biblical Lazarus, and the warm rich man inside to Dives. The draft cuts the entire setup passage (the Euroclydon/Lazarus/Dives extended digression) but retains the Lazarus sentence. The draft *does* retain the Euroclydon passage immediately before, but in it "Poor Lazarus there" appears with "there" pointing to a curbstone figure who was described in the source but not in the draft. In the draft, the only prior content is the Euroclydon quotation and Ishmael's reflection on his own body as a house. No Lazarus on a curbstone has been mentioned. "Poor Lazarus there" uses "there" as a definite locative reference to a specific figure ("chattering his teeth against the curbstone") who has not been established in the draft.

This is a genuine dangling demonstrative: "there" presupposes a Lazarus-figure the reader has been shown, but the draft has not shown one. A competent reader with no source access would not know who "Lazarus there" refers to spatially — the "there" implies a previously described scene that was cut.
